prompt:
You are a second-family code reviewer. In C:\mh-img read fully: scripts/lane_image_agreement.py (focus on author_year_candidates, build_identity, _AUTHOR_YEAR and their use in run()) and tests/test_lane_image_agreement.py. You may read outputs/k_gap/image_reads/MISSING_TRIAL_IDENTITY.json and outputs/k_gap/image_reads/sources/pubmed_esummary_title_named_trials.json (PubMed metadata). Do NOT read cache/, .image_cache/, docs/reviews, docs/acquisitions, evidence/, or any paper text. Do not edit files or change git state.

Purpose: the census names some missing trials only by a truncated title. build_identity maps the title to exactly one member-record PMID and takes the first-author surname and pub/epub years from PubMed esummary. author_year_candidates then matches an agreed forest-plot row labelled 'Surname Year' to that trial. A wrong match would credit a trial with another trial's numbers, so false positives are the serious failure mode; false negatives are acceptable.

Find real ways a WRONG trial could be matched (or a count misreported). Examples to probe: suffix letters ('Blum 2015a'), 'et al', diacritics/hyphens (e.g. 'Fernández-Serrano' vs 'Fernandez-Serrano'), same surname+year for two different trials across different figures/topics, a title prefix that is a prefix of two records, years from epubdate vs pubdate. Confirm each finding by executing small synthetic python (cd C:/mh-img; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import lane_image_agreement as lia).

Answer JSON only: {"findings":[{"severity":"P0|P1|P2","where":"...","claim":"...","input":"...","expected":"...","actual":"..."}],"verdict":"..."}
